model_b.text: Houttuynia cordata belongs to the Saururaceae family and is a medicinal and edible plant with antibacterial, antitussive, and anti-inflammatory effects, which are closely related to its polysaccharide components. This study employed chemical analysis methods (acid hydrolysis, carbonyl reduction, methylation reaction) and instrumental analysis techniques (UV, FT-IR, HPGPC, GC, GC-MS, NMR) to characterize the structure of Houttuynia cordata polysaccharides, while also analyzing their anti-inflammatory activity through in vitro experiments. The main findings are as follows: Sequential extraction of Houttuynia cordata using hot water, 0.05 mol/L EDTA-2Na solution, 0.2 mol/L NaOH solution, and 1 mol/L NaOH solution yielded four polysaccharide fractions: HBHP, CHHP, DAHP, and CAHP. Chemical composition analysis showed that the sugar contents of the four fractions were 66.4%, 63.2%, 60.6%, and 62.8%, respectively, while their uronic acid contents were 29.6%, 22.6%, 18.5%, and 11.6%, respectively. Monosaccharide composition analysis revealed that HBHP and CHHP consisted of rhamnose, arabinose, glucose, and galactose with molar ratios of 9.7:11.9:10.6:21.4 and 11.3:17.8:7.6:18.9, respectively, whereas DAHP and CAHP were composed of arabinose, xylose, glucose, and galactose with molar ratios of 14.1:17.0:9.0:13.8 and 6.6:37.5:9.9:6.3, respectively. Scanning electron microscopy results indicated that HBHP, CHHP, and DAHP had relatively large specific surface areas. Thermogravimetric analysis showed that CAHP exhibited the best thermal stability. Further purification of HBHP using DEAE Cellulose-52 yielded homogeneous polysaccharides HBHP-3 and HBHP-4, with molecular weights of 397.4 kDa and 616.7 kDa, respectively, and uronic acid contents of 20.9% and 14.8%, respectively. Monosaccharide composition analysis demonstrated that the molar ratios of rhamnose, arabinose, glucose, galactose, and galacturonic acid in HBHP-3 and HBHP-4 were 16.0:12.6:4.6:18.1:15.6 and 34.1:6.9:5.0:16.2:10.0, respectively. Structural analysis revealed that the backbone of HBHP-3 consisted of →2)-α-D-Rhap-(1→, →4)-α-D-GalpA-(1→, and →4)-β-D-Galp-(1→, with branches of α-L-Araf-(1→, →5)-α-L-Araf-(1→, →4)-α-D-Glcp-(1→, →6)-β-D-Galp-(1→, and β-D-Galp-(1→ attached at the O-4 position of →2)-α-D-Rhap-(1→. The backbone of HBHP-4 was composed of →2)-α-D-Rhap-(1→, →4)-α-D-GalpA-(1→, and →4)-β-D-Galp-(1→, with branches of α-L-Araf-(1→, →4)-α-D-Glcp-(1→, and β-D-Galp-(1→ attached at the O-4 position of →2)-α-D-Rhap-(1→. Antioxidant activity studies showed that, within the tested concentration range, Houttuynia cordata polysaccharides exhibited good antioxidant activity, with HBHP displaying the best hydroxyl radical and DPPH radical scavenging activities, while DAHP showed the highest ABTS radical scavenging activity and Fe²⁺ chelating ability. Immunomodulatory analysis indicated that all four fractions possessed good immunomodulatory activity, which was positively correlated with polysaccharide concentration. Among them, HBHP had the most pronounced effect on macrophage activation, significantly enhancing phagocytosis. Anti-inflammatory results demonstrated that, within the concentration range of 5–100 μg/mL, HBHP-3 and HBHP-4 inhibited NO secretion and reduced the mRNA expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines in a dose-dependent manner, indicating their significant inhibitory effects on LPS-induced cellular inflammatory responses. Western blot analysis revealed that HBHP-3 exerted its anti-inflammatory activity by suppressing the phosphorylation levels of NF-κB protein (p65) and IκBα.
